text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Economy Minister Augusto Mateus takes full responsibility for the success or failure of the so-called "Mateus Plan" to help ailing companies.

- The direct sale was 17 times subscribed and the public offer for sale (OPV) was three times subscribed in the flotation of a 35.6 percent stake in mobile phone operator Telecel, Lisbon bourse officials said.
- Brussels is cutting a range of agriculture subsidies to Portugal in 1996, an agriculture ministry source said.
- Cement company Cimpor may buy a new cement company in Brazil this year, the paper learned.
- The value of oil company Petrogal is estimated at between 220 and 230 billion escudos, an informed source told the paper. Saudi Aramco is negotiating to become a strategic partner of Petrogal.
- 55 percent of Portuguese adolescent females in the age range 16 to 19 do not go to school, an OECD report says.
- Telecel shares will be admitted to Lisbon's stock exchange today after yesterday's successful flotation.
- The Portuguese government and unions ended a round of talks on Monday with no accord in sight on public sector wages.
